---
title: "Playful indicators"
description: "Hearts, glasses, plants, flames and flowers."
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(ddplot)
```

Illustrative SVG indicators. They show a single level and are meant for presentations, landing pages and dashboards that need a lighter touch.

::: {.dd-chooser}

| Chart | Use it when |
|---|---|
| [`heart_fill()`](#heart_fill) | You show a level from 0 to 1 as a filling heart |
| [`glass_fill()`](#glass_fill) | You show a level from 0 to 1 as a filling glass |
| [`plant_growth()`](#plant_growth) | You show progress as a growing plant |
| [`flame()`](#flame) | You show an intensity, such as an error count, as a flame |
| [`flower()`](#flower) | You want a decorative, optionally rotating, flower |

:::

## `heart_fill()` {#heart_fill}

The `heart_fill` function allows you to display a heart indicator which will be filled according to a numerical value from 0 to 1: 

```{r}
heart_fill(fill_level = 0.8, titleText = NULL, renderFillLabel = FALSE)
```

## `glass_fill()` {#glass_fill}

The `glass_fill` function works the same way as the `heart_fill` above: 

```{r}
glass_fill(fill_level = 0.8, titleText = "Glass of water", renderFillLabel = TRUE)
```

## `plant_growth()` {#plant_growth}

The `plant_growth` function can also be used as a visual clue: 

```{r}
plant_growth(0.4)
```
```{r}
plant_growth(1)
```

## `flame()` {#flame}

You can create cool `flames` using the `flame` function, useful if you want to display the state of a critical information that yields a numerical values (for example, the number of errors encountered in a specific process):

```{r}
flame(
  intensity = 20, 
  flameGradientColors = c("yellow", "orange", "darkred"),
  flameOutline = "darkred",
  bgcol = "#fefefe"
)
```

```{r}
flame(
  intensity = 80, 
  flameGradientColors = c("green", "darkgreen", "darkblue"),
  flameOutline = "#fefefe",
  bgcol = "black"
)
```

## `flower()` {#flower}

The `flower()` function allows you to plot a simple flowers with a defined number of petals. You can also define the width/length of the petals and rotate them if needed: 

```{r}
flower(
  petalCount = 7,
  petalColor = "plum",
  rotationSpeed = 0
)
```

```{r}
flower(
  petalCount = 15,
  petalWidth = 20,
  petalColor = "plum",
  rotationSpeed = 1.5
)
```
